sources.title: GitHub Actions: Using artifact attestations to establish provenance for builds
sources.finding: GitHub supports artifact attestations with SPDX SBOM linkage; P0-013 generates inventory and provenance hooks only and does not create a release attestation.

sources.title: GitHub Actions setup-dotnet
sources.finding: The official action can install the SDK described by global.json and requires only contents: read for the selected non-publishing workflow.

sources.title: GitHub Actions checkout
sources.finding: Checkout fetches the triggering repository revision; credentials can be disabled after checkout for a read-only security workflow.

sources.title: Trivy Action
sources.finding: The official Trivy action scans public container image references and can fail CI at selected vulnerability severities without credentials.

sources.title: NIST Secure Software Development Framework 1.1
sources.finding: The P0 baseline records machine-readable dependency and provenance evidence and applies repeatable security checks before later release scope.

sources.title: SLSA v1.2
sources.finding: Release provenance remains a later release-integrity operation; this work provides a local checksum/provenance hook rather than a release claim.

decision: Use dependency-free local PowerShell controls plus the installed .NET package reporting capability for SAST-style policy, SCA, secret, Compose policy, SPDX inventory, and checksum/provenance evidence. Use immutable-pinned GitHub Actions only for read-only CI and public Compose-image vulnerability scans. Do not introduce a product image build, secret, deployment credential, release publication, or release attestation in P0.
limitations: The local SAST control is a narrow, explicit source-policy baseline; it is not a substitute for later language-aware code scanning or penetration testing.
The generated SPDX inventory and provenance JSON are local/CI evidence hooks, not signed attestations, release approvals, or production deployment evidence.
The image-vulnerability action executes only in GitHub Actions after protected integration; no container pull, image scan, or external publishing is started locally by this work.
Refresh all selected action, scanner, and standards references before changing pipeline or release scope.
